tasks.short: Check that each endoscope's reprocessing is complete, run safety checks on the equipment, record the checks, and take faulty equipment out of use and report it.

steps.what: Endoscopy technician checks that each endoscope's reprocessing record is complete before use
Endoscopy technician performs safety checks to verify proper equipment functioning
Endoscopy technician records the checks on the paper checklist
Endoscopy technician takes faulty equipment out of use and reports it: by phone today; after the change writes a work order from the tracking screen and calls only for urgent faults
Endoscopy technician checks the work order: device, fault found and urgency
Endoscopy technician submits the checked work order to medical technology

tasks.design: Scanning an endoscope's serial number in the scope tracking system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows its last reprocessing cycle and blocks scopes without a valid cycle, so the technician does not look up paper records. The safety checklist runs on a tablet per device and stores the result with the device. Faults are written from the same screen as a work order for medical technology with the device and fault; the technician checks it and submits it once, and only urgent faults need a call. The safety checks themselves stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reprocessing and checks were on paper and faults reported by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Scope tracking systems link reprocessing cycles, checks and work orders per device.
tasks.still_hard: Loan equipment is not in the system.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that an angulation wheel is stiffer than it should be.

evidence.claim: Scope tracking systems can link reprocessing cycles, checklists and fault reports to each endoscope.
Reprocessing of each endoscope must be traceable to the patient it was used on.

assumptions: Boundary: from the procedure list to the fault reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: washers send cycle data to the tracking system; fallback is paper.

Safety checks do not get shorter. s3 keeps 80 because the tablet lists the checks per device and the technician still records each result; s4 keeps 60 because taking equipment out of use and writing the fault stay; the work order check and submit keep their full time.
Medical technology reads work orders as it took calls.
research_questions: Are scopes without a valid cycle ever used?

incremental.description: Endoscopy technician enters loan equipment by hand.

approvals.approved_version: The work order with device, fault and urgency exactly as checked by the technician in s4b, submitted once to medical technology's queue; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small unit with few scopes and washers not all linked, so s1 keeps 60 and s4 keeps 80 (9.1); high: a large unit with many lists a day (14.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count supplies in the storeroom, keep the stock list, decide what to reorder, fill the order, check it, send it, and store deliveries.

steps.what: Endoscopy technician counts endoscopic equipment and supplies in the storeroom: a full count today, spot checks after the change
Endoscopy technician scans the card of each empty bin
Endoscopy technician maintains the inventory list on paper
Endoscopy technician decides what to reorder
Endoscopy technician fills the order in the hospital purchasing system
Endoscopy technician checks the final order: items and quantities against the coming lists, items outside the bins, and the purchasing account
Endoscopy technician submits the checked order to purchasing in one release
Endoscopy technician receives and stores deliveries

tasks.design: Supplies sit in a two-bin system with barcode cards; when a bin is empty its card is scanned, which updates stock in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}) and adds the item to an order list, so the paper list is not kept and counts become spot checks. The technician adjusts quantities and decides on items outside the bins; the technician checks the order and submits it once to purchasing. Storing deliveries stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was counted by eye, kept on paper and orders typed in item by item.
tasks.enabler_now: Two-bin scanning feeds hospital purchasing systems.
tasks.still_hard: Expensive single items need separate handling.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a heavy list of procedures is coming next week.
tasks.altitude: The technician decides orders instead of counting.

evidence.claim: Two-bin systems with barcode cards can feed stock and order lists in hospital purchasing systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock round to supplies stored; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: bins and minimum levels set; fallback is the paper list.
The technician checks every order. Scanning bin cards (s1s) keeps its full time; s1 keeps 50 for spot checks; s6 keeps 20 for the release.
research_questions: Do cancelled procedures due to missing supplies fall?

incremental.description: No separate new work: scanning empty bin cards is shown in s1s.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items and quantities exactly as checked by the technician in s5, submitted once to purchasing in the purchasing system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many single items outside the bins, so s1 keeps 80 and s4 keeps 70 (26.8); high: mostly standard disposables in bins (40.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sign up for in-service training, attend it, pass the practical skills test, and file the certificate in the competence file.

steps.what: Endoscopy technician signs up for training sessions by e-mail
Endoscopy technician attends in-service training to refresh professional skills
Endoscopy technician takes the practical skills test with the assessor
Assessor records the practical sign-off in the learning system
Endoscopy technician files the certificate in the personal competence file: by hand today; after the change checks the sign-off in the learning system

tasks.design: The learning system ({LMS}) tracks each technician's device competences with expiry dates and enrols them in the next session before a competence expires, so sign-up is not arranged by e-mail. The assessor records the practical sign-off in the same system, so certificates are not filed by hand. Training and the skills test stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sign-ups were by e-mail and certificates filed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems track competences with expiry dates.
tasks.still_hard: Manufacturer training outside the hospital is not in the system.
tasks.human_edge: Practising a rare emergency procedure on a model.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can track competences per device with expiry dates and record sign-offs.
Hospitals must be able to show that staff are trained on the medical devices they use.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training due to the certificate filed; designing training is outside.
Input contract: competences and expiry dates set up; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Training and tests do not change.
Assessors record sign-offs in about the time a paper certificate took (s3a, other-role time). s1 keeps 30 for checking the enrolment; s4 keeps 30 for checking the sign-off.
research_questions: Are expired competences found before an audit?

incremental.description: Endoscopy technician uploads certificates of outside training.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few long courses outside the learning system, so s1 keeps 70 and s4 keeps 60 (6.5); high: many short device trainings (13.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare materials on equipment, run the in-service session, test participants' skills, and record attendance and sign-offs.

steps.what: Endoscopy technician prepares session materials on equipment or instruments
Endoscopy technician conducts in-service training sessions on equipment or instruments
Participants sign in to the session with the QR code
Endoscopy technician tests participants' practical skills and signs them off
Endoscopy technician records attendance and sign-offs: on paper lists today; after the change records sign-offs in the learning system while attendance comes from the sign-in

tasks.design: Session materials per device are kept in a shared library with the manufacturer's instructions ({DOCS}) and reused, instead of being made per session. Participants sign in by QR code and the technician records sign-offs in the learning system ({LMS}), so paper lists are not kept. Teaching and testing stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were rebuilt per session and attendance kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems take QR sign-in and record sign-offs.
tasks.still_hard: New devices come with little training material.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a colleague how a scope should feel in the hand.

reach.learn: Whether training happens before first use.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can take QR sign-in and record practical sign-offs.
Hospitals must be able to show that staff are trained on the medical devices they use.

assumptions: Boundary: from new equipment to attendance recorded; buying equipment is outside.
Input contract: sessions set up in the learning system; fallback is paper.
Teaching and testing do not change. Participants sign in by QR code (s2q, other-role time). s4 keeps 60 because the sign-in replaces the attendance list and each sign-off is still recorded.
research_questions: Are all users trained before first use?

incremental.description: Endoscopy technician keeps the materials library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off sessions on new devices, so materials are made new and s1 keeps 95 (4.1); high: repeated sessions on the same equipment (9.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The endoscopy technician keeps checking equipment, deciding orders, training and teaching; paper checklists, stock lists, e-mailed sign-ups and paper attendance lists shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time at the procedure.
